Terms

These terms of use cover the Veylet Capture app and the Veylet Studio service, for Veylet Studio (Australia). Last updated 25 September 2026. Applying, requesting a walkthrough or completing a first sign-in when account access is available (which creates the email account) is not approval, a booking or a paid contract. This is not legal advice.

Capturing and sharing a space. You must have permission to capture and share a space, and you must hold the rights to anything you upload. Do not upload other people’s private interiors without that permission, and keep street addresses, access codes and identity documents out of Veylet records — the desk rejects an address-shaped location for that reason. Concept imagery on this site is original and AI-generated. It is not a captured property or a client case study.

The free months. An eligible new account gets 3 free months with 6 accepted walkthroughs included across them, on the Veylet plan monthly or annual. Starting them needs a payment method on file. Nothing is charged during them unless the account owner buys a pack or a Super fast render. The first charge is on the day they end, at the price of the plan you chose; if you cancel before then, nothing is charged. There is one trial per agency (ABN) and workspace, and real captures unlock in the app once your practice room passes. Fair use: up to 12 render attempts during the free months, including retries. Eligibility is confirmed when the plan is activated: by Apple for the App Store, by us when a card is saved on this website, or in the studio's written terms for an invoiced account. A walkthrough counts as accepted when the automatic quality check passed and your account approved that exact revision; a capture that was not good enough never counts. More walkthroughs during the free months come only from a walkthrough pack the account owner chooses to buy. Using the 6 does not end your free months early or authorise an automatic charge.

The plan’s walkthroughs. After the free months, the Veylet plan monthly includes 2 accepted walkthroughs per monthly allowance window; unused ones roll over, up to 4 banked at any time. The Veylet plan annual includes 24 accepted walkthroughs to use any time in the plan year, with no monthly limit; the pool resets on each plan-year anniversary, and unused ones do not carry into the next year. If you choose annual before your free months end, your first plan year includes 4 bonus walkthroughs, 28 in total, and 4 Super fast renders, once per workspace; Super fast renders are used on this website. Existing Team or Office plans keep their agreed allowance.

Your first walkthrough. If your first walkthrough isn’t listing-ready, we redo it free. This covers your account’s first accepted walkthrough: the redo is a correction on the same link and uses no walkthrough. A new capture visit is not included. This promise is in addition to your rights under the Australian Consumer Law.

Referrals. When an office you refer becomes a paying account, your account and theirs each get 1 bonus walkthrough. You share your own referral link; each referred office is credited once.

Counting walkthroughs. One walkthrough covers up to 8 rooms of one property, counted automatically from your capture; each further 8 rooms uses one more. Every property gets one link and one QR code. A correction of the same walkthrough, or a recapture of the rooms the quality check names, uses none.

Walkthrough packs. The account owner can buy a pack of 3 or 10 walkthroughs, during the free months or on the plan: 3 walkthroughs for A$169 or 10 for A$499, as on the offer page. A pack’s walkthroughs are used only after the walkthroughs your free months or plan include, and they expire 12 months after purchase; walkthroughs unused by then are not refunded. Pack walkthroughs are added once payment has settled: by studio invoice today, and by card in your account once card payment on this website opens. In the app, packs arrive in a later version.

Super fast renders. On this website the account owner can ask for a Super fast render of a capture that has been sent, for A$29 or one Super fast render from the early-annual bonus. It goes first in the queue on the fastest GPU available in Australia and is ready for review in about 30 minutes, any day and any time. If it is not ready within 30 minutes of the upload finishing, the A$29 is refunded automatically, or the Super fast render is returned. There is no daily limit. Super fast is sold only while fast GPUs in Sydney are starting quickly; when they aren’t, your account says “Super fast isn’t available right now” and nothing is charged. An order already paid keeps its promise. Super fast renders are not sold in the app.

Activating. The free months start when you activate the plan with a payment method on file, not when your first walkthrough is accepted: in the app through Apple’s 3-month free introductory offer, with a card saved in Square’s own card field in your account on this website, or through the studio for an account it invoices, on a paid start date agreed in writing. Veylet never sees or stores your card number. Card payment on this website is coming later; until it is available, a plan not started in the app is arranged and invoiced by the studio under agreed terms.

Renewal. The Veylet plan is A$99 a month or A$990 a year by card or studio invoice, and A$119.99 a month or A$1,199.99 a year in the App Store. The first charge is on the day your free months end; a card saved on this website is charged that day and then each month, or each year if you chose annual, until you cancel. An App Store subscription renews automatically each month after its introductory offer at the monthly price shown by Apple before purchase, or each year at the annual price if you chose annual, unless cancelled through Apple. The App Store sells the Veylet plan monthly and annual. An annual plan by studio invoice is billed when the free months end, and an annual invoice is charged in full and covers twelve paid months. Check your renewal date in Settings › Subscriptions or in your account. A reminder email 7 days before the first charge is planned but not running yet, so do not rely on one. Studio-invoiced plans follow the written billing agreement. Changing a renewal preference does not buy extra capacity or promise an earlier paid start. The offer page shows both channels' published prices.

Cancelling. Cancel any time. If you activated in the App Store, cancel in Settings › Subscriptions on the iPhone or iPad signed in to that App Store account; Apple shows the effective end date, including any effect on an introductory offer. For a card plan on this website or an invoiced plan, cancel by email to yoda@yodalai.xyz, and we confirm the date the plan ends. Cancelling stops the next charge and nothing else. Every released walkthrough stays live while your account has a running plan (free months, monthly or annual). When the plan ends, its link, embed and QR code keep working for 14 days, then go offline; they are not deleted or revoked, and restarting the plan brings the same links back at once. To keep a single walkthrough online without a plan, ask us for a hosting extension: A$49 a year per walkthrough. Deleting the Veylet account ends its hosting. It does not cancel an Apple subscription; manage that separately through Apple. Cancellation is not required to request account deletion.

Other work. Editing and hosting extensions are priced on the offer page. They are charged only for work you asked for and we agreed in writing first.

Refunds. A purchase made through the App Store is Apple’s sale. Apple refunds it under its own policy and we cannot refund or reverse it: ask Apple through its Report a Problem page. A charge made on the website is refunded in full if you ask within 14 days of that charge and no walkthrough was accepted in the period it paid for. For a walkthrough pack, that rule applies only while none of its walkthroughs was used, and a refund removes the pack’s unused walkthroughs. Nothing here limits your rights under the Australian Consumer Law.

Deleting your account. Ask in the app or on your desk at veylet.com/account. We complete the deletion within 30 days and confirm when it is done. You cannot undo it yourself. When it completes, your account, its spaces and its walkthroughs are removed, every handoff link and embed stops working, and hosting of every released walkthrough ends with them — deletion ends hosting at once, without the 14 days that follow the end of a plan. Remove the links and embeds from your listing too, because copies people already downloaded cannot be recalled.

What deletion covers. Hosted capture files, generated walkthroughs and the account records used to deliver them are removed. Once removal starts, these files cannot be restored through your account. Copies on your own device, exported files and copies already downloaded by someone else are outside this account deletion. Contact us about any copies held separately by the studio.

Limited records we retain. Invoices, receipts and minimal records of payments, accepted services and deletion may be retained for accounting and legal obligations. These retained records do not provide access to your imagery, captures or walkthroughs. Deleting a Veylet account does not cancel a subscription billed by Apple; manage that subscription in your Apple account.

No promise of work. Veylet does not promise jobs, leads or earnings to operators or to capture partners. Applying is free assessment; it does not create an account, grant app access, take payment or reserve capacity.

Australian Consumer Law. Our services come with guarantees that cannot be excluded under the Australian Consumer Law. Nothing in these terms excludes, restricts or modifies them. For a major failure you are entitled to a refund; where the failure is not major, you are entitled to have the problem fixed within a reasonable time.

GST and currency. Every amount is in Australian dollars. If GST applies it is included in the price shown, and the receipt states the exact treatment. Apple is the merchant of record for App Store subscriptions and remits Australian GST on those sales; Apple’s receipt, not ours, is the tax invoice for them.

Governing law. These terms are governed by the law of Queensland, Australia, and the courts of Queensland have jurisdiction.
